A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TS-roots research. Their main texts, equations, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison across the reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark optimization, inner-loop comparisons, MES experiments, and sample-average sensitivity results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds truss optimization, starting-point diagnostics, and comparisons with grid and Latin hypercube initialization.

M1.justification: Equation (4) changes exploitation-point ranking from posterior-mean values in v1 to posterior-sample values in v2, also specified in Appendix D. The remaining rootfinding and sample-average procedures are retained. Algorithm 1's comment still says posterior mean, leaving an implementation ambiguity despite the documented rule change.

E1.justification: v2 adds one ten-variable structural-design problem: minimizing a weighted combination of cross-sectional area and displacement for a ten-bar truss (Appendix G, Figure 2(f)). The existing synthetic functions and dimensions remain.

E2.justification: Figures 10–11 add uniform-grid and Latin hypercube initialization as evaluated inner-loop comparators. Random multistart and genetic-algorithm comparisons remain, as do the outer-loop TS-DSRF, TS-RF, EI, LCB, and MES comparator sets.

E3.justification: The new Appendix D diagnostic uses n_o = 5000, n_e = n_x = 1000, and buffer coefficient 3; the added grid/LHS comparisons show 50-iteration trajectories. Existing main-experiment settings, including n_e = 250 and n_x = 200, remain. Newly reporting n_o = 500 does not establish a change to those existing experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix D and Figure 7 introduce a substantial diagnostic of which ranked exploration and exploitation starts reach the best multistart solution across five functions. This directly investigates minimum useful set sizes and supports smaller-budget recommendations, whereas v1 left subset-size effects to future work. The existing sample-average sensitivity study is retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report medians and interquartile ranges from 20 runs for the main benchmark and sample-average studies, and ten runs for MES. No revised repetition counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance procedures are reported. The new start-rank histograms describe diagnostic outcomes rather than uncertainty in performance estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial result sets: truss optimization curves favoring TS-roots in Figure 2(f), successful-start rank distributions in Figure 7, and grid/LHS comparisons in Figures 10–11 showing stronger high-dimensional acquisition optimization and runtime performance. These are additional findings, not demonstrated improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: Appendix C.5 adds a conditional whole-algorithm complexity derivation combining posterior evaluation, gradient optimization, and minimum-selection costs, concluding O(dn + dθ) under fixed-budget assumptions. The existing local-minimum proposition and proof, counting formulas, rootfinding theorem, and sample-average derivation remain.

C1.justification: The abstract newly claims that very small starting sets, even one point from each set, usually discover the global optimum. It also separates GP-TS optimization gains from entropy-search benefits more carefully. The principal TS-roots and sample-average contributions remain; linear scaling and breaking dimensionality's curse were already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly qualifies the MES application: TS-roots supplies optimized posterior samples but does not optimize the MES acquisition function itself. Appendix D additionally interprets successful-start ranks as largely independent of iteration and dimension, motivating smaller set sizes. Existing mechanism explanations and the unresolved choice of the sample-average control parameter remain.

D1.justification: Appendix H newly discloses n_o = 500, and Appendix C.2 specifies recursive subdivision above polynomial degree 100. Appendix G supplies truss loads, material constants, variable bounds, normalization constants, and objective weights. The main code link, hardware descriptions, and other retained experimental settings are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to entropy search, Wilson et al.'s pathwise-conditioning work, and Hoffman and Ribak's Gaussian-field conditioning work. It also expands the distinction between log-reformulated acquisition optimization and optimizing posterior paths with many local minima. These are limited positioning additions; most reference changes are formatting.

P1.justification: The existing sample-average derivation moves from Results into a standalone Section 4. The abstract and pathwise-conditioning background are expanded, and method wording and appendix organization are refined. Most existing prose and the overall argumentative structure remain.

P2.justification: Figure 2 gains a sixth panel, and v2 adds the multi-panel starting-rank diagnostic, truss schematic, and two initialization-comparison figures. A new main-text Algorithm 1 summarizes TS-roots, while existing displays are redistributed and renumbered. This substantially expands the visual presentation without replacing the document template.

improvement.justification: The truss experiment, grid/LHS comparisons, and starting-point diagnostics strengthen support for the existing contribution, while added settings and cost analysis improve transparency. The gain is limited by the empirical best-multistart reference underlying the small-set optimality claims and the conflicting posterior-mean comment in Algorithm 1. The core theoretical foundations and existing results remain.
